cards.honma-premium: Honma has been hand-finishing clubs in Sakata since 1959, and the Beres line is where that work gets expensive. Malbon’s version runs fourteen clubs in black and gold for men and pink and gold for women, with headcovers and a bag included. Forbes reported in January that the sets were selling. Honma moves them through its own US store rather than Malbon’s, and they remain in stock.
cards.honma-performance: The Performance set is built on Honma’s Beres NX platform, in a deep emerald for men and a rose-gold-accented finish for women, fourteen clubs with the same included bag treatment. At $5,800 it is the cheaper half of the Honma collaboration and the one review outlets actually got their hands on, with MyGolfSpy calling the collab “culturally curated.” Honma still has it in stock.
cards.bet-fatcat: Bettinardi milled fifteen of these in March 2022, and every one shipped with an NFT attached — the first putter ever sold that way. The head is double-aged stainless, Bettinardi’s DASS stock, milled softer and scarcer than the steel used on standard runs, with the Fat Cat Buckets character engraved across the flange. Fifteen units is the entire population.
cards.bet-qb6: The Malbon putter story starts here, in May 2021, with nine units and the first Bettinardi collaboration either brand had done. The head is a double-aged stainless QB6 with a hand-formed fancy coil neck and the Wizard Buckets character on the face. The two houses are still dropping together in 2026, and all of it descends from these nine putters.
cards.bet-3step: Bettinardi’s April 2026 Hive release carried two five-unit Malbon runs, and this is the first of them: Buckets in a fedora, doing mid-century mobster. The finish is Tour Blast on a 3-Step Jam neck, a tour-department build rather than a paint job on a retail head. Five were made, and they went the morning the drop opened.
cards.bet-ss3: The second Gangster run is a wide-body SS3 mallet in blacked-out Ox finish, cut to the same five units and released in the same April 2026 Hive drop. It sold out just as fast. Between the two one-of-fives and the maroon plaid INOVAI, Bettinardi’s 2026 Malbon releases were the most limited putters either brand put out all year.
cards.rollking-remington: Bettinardi is not Malbon’s only putter partner. Roll King, a small-batch milling operation, builds the Wiz Buckets editions: a silver mallet with the wizard character engraved on the crown, sold directly through Malbon’s own site. Unlike the Bettinardi runs above it, the Remington is something you can put in your bag today.
cards.rollking-luciano: The Luciano is the blade to the Remington’s mallet, same $1,695, same Wiz Buckets engraving. The first Roll King release with Malbon arrived in July 2024, forty numbered units packed in birch crates, and the current silver editions sit in open stock. A heel-toe blade from a boutique mill costs less here than a one-of-five Bettinardi resells for.
cards.jc-golf-bag: Nothing on Malbon’s own store costs more than this. The 2.0 is a water-treated denim-and-leather carry bag in the collaboration’s latte, green and pink monogram, with an embroidered Buckets on the side. The first Jimmy Choo bag landed in April 2024 alongside a collection that lost ten of its twenty-seven pieces in half an hour, and the 2.0 is still buyable.
cards.jc-sunday-bag: A Sunday bag is the format invented for carrying six clubs and nothing else, which makes $3,250 either the funniest or the most honest number in the whole collaboration. This one is monogram canvas with leather trim, from the April 2025 2.0 collection and since delisted from Malbon’s store. That works out to about $540 per club carried.
cards.jc-duffle: The duffle is the piece nobody wrote headlines about, and it outpriced almost everything else in the collaboration: a full monogram body with green leather trim at $2,095, more than the TAG Heuer watch and more than every putter except the Fat Cat. It sold on Malbon’s site through the 2.0 run and has since left the catalogue, with the price surviving only on the archived product page.
cards.jc-shoebag: The crystal-embellished shoe bag comes from the original April 2024 collection: a leather bag for carrying golf shoes, finished with Jimmy Choo’s crystal work. It is the piece that made the first drop read as real Jimmy Choo rather than a licensing exercise, and it sold out at Malbon accordingly. Golf Digest put the price at $1,275 in its first look.
cards.jc-diamond-womens: Jimmy Choo built an actual spiked golf shoe here — green-trimmed leather with the house’s diamond-pattern sole treatment adapted for turf. It stays listed on Malbon’s store with every size gone. The 2024 originals came in five colorways and were the fastest sellers of the launch.
cards.jc-diamond-mens: The men’s build is white leather with a green heel tab and monogram detailing, at the same $850 the women’s pair carried, verified against Malbon’s own archived listing. For scale, $850 is Jones Sports Co stand bag money spent on one pair of golf shoes, and they sold anyway at that number.
cards.jc-slide: The slide is a $750 pool sandal in the collaboration monogram, with an embroidered Buckets in a bucket hat sitting over the toe. It has nothing to do with golf and everything to do with the clubhouse afterwards, which is the clearest answer to what the Jimmy Choo partnership is actually for. Malbon still has it in stock.
cards.jc-driver-cover: The driver cover is a cylindrical monogram sleeve at $625, more than most drivers cost on the street a season after release. Malbon sold it through the collaboration collection and has since delisted it, and the $625 comes from the brand’s own archived page rather than a resale listing.
cards.tag-malbon: TAG Heuer handed its connected golf watch to Malbon in February 2024, with eighteen bezel markings for eighteen holes, a Buckets face that shifts color as the seconds pass, and shot-tracking and caddie-style hole data built in. It arrived on Malbon’s site alongside a small apparel capsule and has since left the catalogue. No other watch has carried the Buckets logo.
cards.monzee-camo: The ROBA is a full custom plush character, limbs and face and attitude, covered in an abstract camo print that Malbon notes varies from piece to piece. That is the polite way of saying each one is cut differently on purpose. At $1,500 it is the most expensive headcover the brand has ever stocked, and the camo version is somehow still available.
cards.monzee-black: The blackout ROBA is the same character rendered in all-black plush, horned and vaguely demonic in the best way, and it is the half of the pair that sold out. Malbon stocked both at $1,500. For a read on where headcover culture sits in 2026, the black plush monster went before the camo did.
cards.potr-transcon: POTR is the younger line from Yoshida & Co., the Tokyo house behind Porter, whose bags hold roughly the cultural slot in Japan that Malbon holds in LA. The Transcon arrived in January 2023 as a black ballistic golf bag sold only through Porter’s Japanese channels at ¥129,800, never restocked and never released in the US at all. Money helps less with this one than with anything else here.
cards.bet-inovai: The INOVAI was the volume release of the April 2026 Gangster drop, which still meant selling out in a morning. Bettinardi wrapped a 6.0 mallet in maroon plaid and matched it with a mag-closure cover, making it the loudest thing the shop milled all year. At $900 it was also the cheapest way anyone got into the Gangster Buckets release.
cards.xo-rod: The Epitome MB725 is a US-built bass fishing rod with carbon guides and an integrated carbon reel seat, released through Malbon’s May 2026 “Golf & Bass” drop. The reasoning runs same customer, same Saturday, different body of water, which is either brilliant or completely unhinged. Malbon still has it in stock.
cards.bettinardi-cartbag: The putter partnership runs to a cart bag as well, a polyurethane leather-look shell in tan and navy panelling with both logos riding together. Malbon priced it at $498, in line with its own house cart bags, and it sold out anyway. It stays the only bag the two brands have built together.
cards.knicks-varsity: The Garden jacket has a wool body, contrast leather sleeves, Knicks orange-and-blue blocking and a Buckets heart across the back, from Malbon’s NBA run. A golf brand selling a $498 basketball varsity jacket says most of what needs saying about where Malbon sits in 2026. Malbon has it in stock at Madison Square Garden prices.

kickers.1: Clubs are where golf hides its real money, and Malbon keeps three equipment partners: Honma in Sakata, Bettinardi in Chicago and Roll King. Between them sit the most expensive Malbon item ever sold and the most limited, nine units from 2021.
kickers.2: Two collections, April 2024 and the 2.0 run a year later, put a luxury shoemaker’s monogram on golf bags, spiked shoes and slides. Ten of the first drop’s twenty-seven pieces went inside thirty minutes, and most of it has since been delisted.
kickers.3: The strangest shelf in the archive holds a Swiss connected watch, two $1,500 plush creatures, a Japan-only Porter golf bag, a plaid putter and a bass fishing rod. This is the stuff that makes the brand collectible rather than merely successful.
kickers.4: The cheapest tier still costs as much as a full Sunday-bag setup from most independent brands. Two very different ways to spend $498 — one gone from the catalogue, one still in stock.
